newsitem.title: USA: Hillary Clinton wishes Williams hadn't taken check.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton wishes Williams hadn't taken check.

text.p: Hillary Rodham Clinton said Monday her chief of staff Maggie Williams had acted legally in accepting a political donation at the White House but that she wished Williams had not done so "for her sake".

Mrs. Clinton also said she did not know why the Asian-American donor who gave Williams the check, Johnny Chung, had visited the White House so often but that her staff always sought to be polite to visitors.

"She's an honourable and courteous person and what she did was legal and proper under the prevailing rules," Mrs Clinton said of Williams, who accepted the $50,000 donation from Chung in March 1995 and passed it on to the Democratic National Committee.

"But given the concern that it has raised, I'm sure she wishes she had said (to Chung), go mail it or go walk it over" to the DNC, Mrs Clinton said. Asked if she wished Williams had done so, she said, "For her sake, certainly." The first lady spoke in a session with reporters.

Federal law bars government employees from accepting campaign contributions on government property. But the White House says that Williams did not break the law because she did not "accept" the money under the definition of the law.

Chung, described as "a hustler" in a memo written by a National Security Council aide after he arranged for several Chinese officials to sit on on a taping of Clinton's weekly radio broadcast, is a lightning rod in a campaign financing controversy dogging Clinton and his Democratic party.
The Democratic National Committee has returned more than $1.5 million in questionable contributions raised by him and two other Chinese-American supporters of Clinton.

"I think that my staff is a polite, and courteous group, and certainly has over the last four years been very willing to be courteous to people who came into the White House," Mrs Clinton said when asked why Chung had been a frequent visitor there last year and often cleared in by her staff.
"It wasn't only people people in my office who admitted him as I'm sure you know. Other people did as well. And I really don't know anything abut why or under what circumstances."
Mrs Clinton said it "never occurred to me" that some foreign governments might be behind some of the political donations to her husband's campaign.
The president said earlier Monday he was kept in the dark about an FBI warning last year that China might try to funnel money into the U.S. election campaign, and is now trying to find out why.
The first lady said she was involved in fund raising for Clinton but did not recall making any fund-raising telephone calls herself.

Asked why her husband had so many people, including political donors, spend the night at the White House, Mrs Clinton said the president counted "thousands if not hundreds of thousands of people among his friends" and would spontaneously invite people to spend the night.
